record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: If a localized time-independent potential W is added to a linearly moving potential, can the additional reflections caused by W be used to solve the inverse-scattering problem with fewer measurements?

evidence.quote: Problem 4- Combined Terms Potential If one adds a localized time independent potential W to the linearly moving potential, can one use the extra reflections from W to solve the problem with less measurements?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Schrödinger equation on the real line
  i∂_t ψ(x,t) = -∂_x^2 ψ(x,t) + V(x,t) ψ(x,t),
with a combined time-dependent potential of the form
  V(x,t) = V_0(x - vt) + W(x),
where V_0 : ℝ → ℝ is a localized (e.g., compactly supported or Schwartz) potential translating with constant velocity v ≠ 0, and W : ℝ → ℝ is a localized time-independent potential. Consider the associated scattering problem: incoming wave packets are sent toward the combined potential and the resulting reflected and transmitted asymptotic data are recorded.

Inverse-scattering question: Given that adding W produces additional reflections (from the static obstacle, as well as from the interaction between the moving bump V_0(· - vt) and W), determine whether these additional reflections can be exploited to reconstruct the pair (V_0, W) from strictly fewer scattering measurements than are required to reconstruct V_0 alone via the moving-potential inverse-scattering scheme. Specifically, identify a class of measurement protocols (e.g., a finite set of incoming wave packets with prescribed momenta or a single incoming plane wave at one energy) under which the data uniquely determine both V_0 and W, and quantify the reduction in the number of independent measurements compared with the pure moving-potential case W ≡ 0.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of this inverse-scattering question for a localized stationary potential added to a uniformly translating potential. Standard inverse-scattering references treat either purely stationary potentials or general time-dependent settings without addressing the measurement-reduction question posed here, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n (Stefanov)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of inverse scattering primarily for stationary potentials; does not address combined moving plus stationary potential measurement-reduction.
status_evidence.claim: No treatment of the specific combined-potential measurement reduction question is found in standard surveys.

status_evidence.title: Inverse scattering transform - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General overview of inverse scattering transform methods, focused on integrable PDEs and stationary scattering data.
status_evidence.claim: General references on inverse scattering do not resolve the specific question for moving plus stationary potentials.
